subject: Drag of a circular cylinder in crossflow by Reynolds-number regime
in_code: ExosphereSimulation CrossflowDrag follows Jorgensen NASA TR R-474 (figs. 1-6), with crossflow Mach and Reynolds dependence; gates F1 in docs/physics/fidelity_gates.md

regimes.source: Wieselsberger via Jorgensen NASA TR R-474 fig. 2
Achenbach (1968), J. Fluid Mech. 34(4):625-639, as quoted in later work
Achenbach (1968) as quoted in J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn. (2024) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167610524001843

starship_terminal_regime.reynolds: about 6e7 to 8e7 at sea level to 4 km
starship_terminal_regime.note: beyond the measured range of Achenbach (5e6); transcritical C_D of 0.5-0.7 is the expected band. Subcritical C_D = 1.2 does not apply.

implication: Broadside drag of a Starship-size hull at terminal speed should use the transcritical crossflow coefficient. A RANS study that does not state its Reynolds number (Li 2022 gives C_D 9.5-11 on base area at 90 deg, about 640 m2 of drag area) may sit in a different regime. The Flight 14 broadcast terminal speed (363 km/h at 1.2 km) fits the lower drag area, within the mass uncertainty.
